title: What's the deal with lack of Voodoo horror movies in the past 5-10 years?

commenti.body:
>We saw a CURSE OF LA LLORONA movie that spoke to latinos<

What does that even mean? I’m from South America and I’m supposed to feel something about that movie being made or what? It sucked ass anyway

The problem there is that "voodoo" is a whole religion, and the horror movie aspects that have shown up in pop culture are apparently very inaccurate and considered offensive.

It would be like if there were a bunch of Hollywood movies that portrayed Jewish people as evil wizards who use scary magic to make your eyeballs explode or something.  Once people realized how weird it was to make all those movies in the first place, they'd be a little hesitant to make any more.
No, I am just saying that they specifically made it for a target demo. Nothing more.
Yeah true but what if they did it where they showed Voodoo as good but there's also scary things in it too? Like SERPENT AND THE RAINBOW.

"Voodoo" as you'd see it in any major media medium is basically just a frankenstein of stereotype fictions, created to sell to ignorant americans. For movie producers and the like, it served its purpose, and once the well was dry, it got dumped for the next

That would have been fine if it started out that way.  Serpent and the Rainbow is a classic, after all.

But, anything they make now is going to be associated with the movies that came before, and any little mistakes they make are going to be conflated with the willful ignorance of those movies.  Maybe a writer/director who grew up in Vodou culture could get away with it, but anybody else is going to end up with more trouble than one little film is worth.
But that purpose was what 20 years ago with Skeleton Key?

Hmm I think they could use stereotypes to subvert audiences expectations. Like you think Voodoo is bad but its actually good and about healing, etc

As someone from Louisiana who has personally known people who practice voodoo, I just don’t think a new horror movie about voodoo is a good idea. The religion has been so demonized and mischaracterized by Hollywood and beyond for racist/colonialist reasons that any film that plays into those stereotypes would most likely be harmful. There’s probably something subversive and interesting you could do if the film was being made by someone with knowledge from that community, but it’s unlikely that kind of film would interest a mainstream studio. Basically, to answer your initial question, Voodoo has too much historical baggage to be disentangled to interest any filmmaker from taking a crack at it.

Agree. If what OP wants is the “exotic religion / scary cult horror” sub genre this is still alive and well — I’d argue that a movie like Midsommar actually hits many of the same notes as a voodoo horror movie, albeit with a very different aesthetic and setting: outsiders brought into the cult and everything seems great until it isn’t.

And of course there are tons of movies within the broader horror subgenre about curses and the occult. Sticking with Ari Aster, we have Hereditary. Or either Suspiria (OG or remake — both good in their own ways).

Going even broader to religious horror, it feels like there’s a new horror movie with Catholic trappings every month, it seems.

But if it’s gotta be “curse based horror movie with a black antagonist from an unspecified West Indian island” then, yeah…. that’s pretty niche.

Great points. I do though think that a horror film that plays on these stereotypes and its actually a rug pull where Voodoo is good and about healing could not only be a surprise story twist, potentially scary, but also help paint Voodoo in a better light.

What do you think?

Yeah that would be interesting. There’s just very few filmmakers I trust to do that. Jordan Peele would probably be the only one who’d really try to dive into the racial context of the religion to inform the horror.
My concern with Peele is that he makes it too much about race .

I don't know what you're talking about on a where they've gone. I'm a fairly avid horror fan and I think I could name just a small handful of films focused on voodoo, I'd be pressed for ten. There were never many. 

I do love the Louisianna setting though, needs to be utilised more. Can't see any reason not to create more, outside of the offensive notion these comments have that we need to treat other cultures with kiddie gloves and depict them as completely good. If it's accurate and effective who cares.

I'm not an expert on Voodoo by any means, but three of my favorite horror movies are from this subgenre: *I Walked with a Zombie*, *The Serpent and the Rainbow*, and *Angel Heart*. I don't really know what the appeal is, but I think it has to do with the fact that supernatural phenomena are somehow grounded in real-life beliefs. I can see how this is a touchy subject and probably the reason why filmmakers don't approach it too often.
